 Clockwatch Premier League Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool, Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea, and more: Premier League – as it happened

 3h ago 11.35 EST Right then, I’ll be off. Please head here to follow the latest from Aston Villa v Manchester United, where there’s been an early goal:
 Manchester United v Aston Villa: Premier League – live Read more And peruse reports on the 2pm Premier League kick-offs here:
 Brighton 2-0 Brentford 
 Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool 
 Ipswich 1-2 Bournemouth 
 Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea 
 Bye!
 Share 3h ago 11.23 EST John Brewin was at the Amex Stadium, where Brighton cantered to victory over 10-man Brentford:
 Who can stop Brighton’s ascension in English and European football? They continue to set standards, practices that leave almost everybody else trailing in their wake. Their second-place position in the Premier League would once have read like a glitch in a Football Manager session.
 Come November 2026, they appear the only team capable of throwing down a challenge to Arsenal. Under low winter sun, Brentford, the club Brighton are often compared to, though one with a different outlook, were readily swatted aside. If Keith Andrews’ team, and their fans at the Amex, might level blame at a couple of refereeing decisions, it was a contest they were given little chance of rescuing anything from.
 Much more here:
 Diego Gómez hits another stunner as Brighton beat 10-man Brentford to go second Read more Share 3h ago 11.21 EST Andy Brassell saw Sunderland inflict a fourth defeat of the league season on Chelsea, the most of any team in the top nine:
 A lot can change in five-and-half months, but as an early winter chill descended on Wearside this week – both meteorologically and metaphorically – Sunderland were determined that some things should remain the same.
 Just as they had beaten Chelsea on the final day of last season in May to ensure European qualification for the first time in 53 years, they did so again on Sunday to lift themselves off the bottom of the Premier League. The real triumph was that a patched-up defence, without the injured Dan Ballard and the banned Omar Alderete, kept Chelsea at enough distance to allow Robin Roefs a tranquil afternoon. Chelsea may be developing into a chaotic must-watch under Xabi Alonso but they were subdued here, and fall out of the top four.
 Much more here:
 Sunderland stun Chelsea as Le Fée’s penalty breathes life into Black Cats Read more Share 3h ago 11.19 EST David Hytner was at Selhurst Park to see Liverpool snaffle three goals and as many points:
 It was the moment when Liverpool knew they would win here in south London and so move on from the Premier League loss to Arsenal at Anfield last Sunday and the one in midweek at Fenerbahce in the Champions League.
 Florian Wirtz had timed his run as Liverpool broke up the right and Bradley Barcola’s low pull back was made to measure. Wirtz had to take it on first time and it was a test of his technique under pressure. He never looked like failing it, not least because smoothness in this area is his calling card. Liverpool were 2-0 up, Alexis Mac Allister having headed them in front towards the end of the first-half, and all you could hear was the eruption of delight in the away supporters’ enclosure.
 Much more here:
 Alexander Isak tops off goal trio for Liverpool as late penalty offers little for Crystal Palace Read more Share 3h ago 11.16 EST A report on Ipswich v Bournemouth: 
 Another Evanilson goal helped fire Marco Rose’s Bournemouth to an eighth straight victory with a hard-fought 2-1 win at Ipswich.
 Evanilson failed to score in his first six appearances of the season but found the net for a fifth consecutive Premier League match and made it seven goals in eight after five minutes at Portman Road.
 More here:
 Evanilson launches eighth straight Bournemouth win as Ipswich blunder Read more Share 3h ago 11.15 EST “Hi Simon,” writes Simon McMahon. Hello! “Couple of games in Scotland today, and get this, Falkirk are 4-0 up away to Hearts after the first 45! They will leapfrog the Tynecastle side into 3rd place, remarkable really for a team who were in Scottish League One only four seasons ago.” They’ve just made it 5-0, Jacob Murrell scoring in the 47th minute.
 Share 3h ago 11.14 EST “As a Manchester United fan, I’m not sure I’ve ever been so disappointed to see Liverpool winning a game,” writes John Brennan. “United could be bottom of league in November. Think of the content, the takes, the banter. Give it to Dychey, Big Sam etc. And with the international break, we would have two whole weeks of it. For shame Liverpool, for shame.”
 Share 3h ago 11.05 EST While I wait for some match reports and post-match reaction, Tim de Lisle is monitoring the Manchester United v Aston Villa game here:

 Share 3h ago 11.02 EST Final score: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea
 Whistles ring out from desperate fans at the Stadium of Light, and after 96 and a bit minutes the referee gets the message! Sunderland secure their second league win of the season!
 View image in fullscreen Sunderland's Granit Xhaka and manager Regis Le Bris celebrate after the match. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters Share Updated at  11.29 EST 3h ago 10.59 EST Kari Tulinius has been monitoring this game. “When Sunderland can start Brobbey, the whole team is coherent,” he writes. “Even after he’s gone off the field, he’s created space for his replacement by tiring out the centre-backs. Chelsea, meanwhile, don’t make sense without João Pedro. They don’t have anyone else who can pull defenses this way and that with intelligence of movement and positioning.”
 Share 3h ago 10.58 EST Also final scores: Brighton 2-0 Brentford; Ipswich 1-2 Bournemouth
 There remains 90 seconds or so of stoppage time to be played at the Stadium of Light, where Sunderland are clinging on to a 1-0 lead.
 Share 3h ago 10.57 EST Final score: Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool
 And that’s the last kick of the game! Victory takes Liverpool to fourth and Palace drop to last place, where they’ll remain at the end of the day unless Aston Villa beat Manchester United by 11 goals or more.
 Share 3h ago 10.55 EST GOAL! Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool (Nketiah, 90+5 mins)
 Alisson goes the right way, but Nketiah finds the side netting!
 Share 3h ago 10.55 EST Penalty to Crystal Palace!
 Kerkez jumps with Osorio for a ball in the box, gets there second and makes contact with the player after the ball has gone. The referee points to the spot!
 Share 3h ago 10.53 EST Since we’ve been on air Algeria’s USM Alger have snaffled the African Super Cup, Ahmed Khaldi scoring one goal and setting up another as they stunned hosts ⁠Mamelodi Sundowns from ⁠South ​Africa with a 3-1 victory at a rain-soaked Loftus Versfeld Stadium. Khaldi curled in ⁠a superb shot from outside the box ​10 minutes into ‌the second ‌half, having set up an early goal ‌for Zakaria Draoui as USM claimed the trophy for the second time after a maiden success in 2023. Saadi Radouani also found the back of the ‌net for the visitors, while Iqraam Rayners’ first-half penalty for Sundowns ​proved a consolation. The start of the second half was delayed by around 30 minutes after a heavy downpour in ⁠Pretoria
 View image in fullscreen Mamelodi Sundowns supporters cheer during the CAF Super Cup final soccer match between Mamelodi Sundowns and USM Alger in Pretoria. Photograph: Themba Hadebe/AP Share 3h ago 10.51 EST GOAL! Crystal Palace 0-3 Liverpool (Isak, 89 mins)
 Now Isak has his goal! Another break in which he combines with Munoz: an excellent pass plays the Spaniard down the right, a low ball infield finds Wirtz and he touches to Isak, who takes his chance expertly!
 View image in fullscreen Liverpool's Alexander Isak scores their third goal. Photograph: Andrew Couldridge/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  10.56 EST 3h ago 10.48 EST Chance for Isak, but Henderson saves! Liverpool break from their own penalty area: Wirtz hoofs the ball clear, Isak and Munoz exchange passes and the Swede carries it to the edge of the area before shooting low, hard, and too close to the keeper.
 Share 3h ago 10.46 EST Munoz tees up Wirtz for another first-time shot, but this one’s too close to Henderson. It hasn’t been an overwhelming performance from Liverpool by any means, but Palace look a beaten side now (cue inevitable comeback).
 Share 3h ago 10.44 EST Munoz throws himself over Lerma’s foot and is rightly booked for diving. Mac Allister confronts Lerma in the aftermath, and both players also end up with yellow cards.
 Share 3h ago 10.41 EST Rio Ngumoha, a 76th-minute substitute, takes an extraordinarily optimistic shot, from maybe three yards short of the byline and 15 yards wide of goal. It had almost no chance of going in even if it was on target, which it very emphatically was not.
 Share 3h ago 10.38 EST Brilliant chance for Crystal Palace! A defensive slip allows Richards to run through on the right and square to Pino, but it’s a bit behind him and he’s forced to take a touch, and by the time he shoots Alisson has raced off his line and the shot hits the keeper!
 Share 3h ago 10.37 EST Team news has dropped for the late Premier League game, and here is is. As it stands Manchester United will start the game in 19th place:
 Man Utd: Lammens, Mazraoui, Yoro, Maguire, Dalot, Tielemans, Mainoo, Diallo, Fernandes, Cunha, Mbeumo. Subs: Darlow, de Ligt, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Santos, Heaven, Lacey, Jack Fletcher.
 Aston Villa: Suzuki, Lindelof, Harwood-Bellis, Torres, Maatsen, Kamara, Goretzka, Alysson, McGinn, Manzambi, Jackson. Subs: Bizot, Mings, Barkley, Buendia, Mbaye, Joao Gomes, Madjo, Cisse, Hemmings.
 Referee: Chris Kavanagh.
 Share 4h ago 10.32 EST GOAL! Ipswich 1-2 Bournemouth (Clarke penalty, 73 mins)
 Another penalty, this time at Ipswich, where Jack Clarke gets the home team back in the game with a very coolly-taken spot-kick.
 Share 4h ago 10.29 EST A double change for Liverpool, who bring Szoboszlai and Barcola off and Munoz and Nyoni on.
 Share 4h ago 10.26 EST Palace are trying, a bit clumsily at present, to find a way back into this game. Osorio tries to find a way past Kerkez, but the Liverpool defender throws himself to the ground and wins a free kick.
 Share 4h ago 10.20 EST Yellow card! The specific thing Barcola was threatening there was Pino’s ankle, and into the book he goes.
 Share 4h ago 10.19 EST Another chance for Liverpool, but Mitchell slides in to block a cross-shot from Barcola, who has switched to the right flank at half-time and looks much more threatening for it.
 Share 4h ago 10.18 EST A point of information from Grant Kempton, regarding the Igor Thiago red card: “Just to correct. Chema was booked ... taken off at half time because of the booking. But its still force into the face so booking and red card sounds right.” Ah fair dos.
 Share 4h ago 10.16 EST GOAL! Crystal Palace 0-2 Liverpool (Wirtz, 54 mins)
 Liverpool double their lead! Barcola is played down the right and sends in a nice low cross, possibly aiming for Isak, but it runs to Wirtz and he strokes it into the corner!
 View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz of Liverpool scores his team’s second goal. Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images Share Updated at  10.27 EST 4h ago 10.10 EST Two players run clear for Crystal Palace, and Wharton just has to slide the ball across for Strand Larsen to turn it in! But his pass is abysmal, Strand Larsen can’t reach it, and he’ll be grateful in the circumstances that he was about 10 yards offside when the ball was played through.
 Share 4h ago 10.08 EST “Re the Thiago sending-off, we saw last week with the shirt-pull on Isak that wasn’t punished precisely why players over-exaggerate,” writes Andy Flintoff. For sure, but if someone hits your chin and you go down holding your forehead, you’re not drawing the referee’s attention to a foul, you’re cheating.
 Share 4h ago 10.07 EST GOAL! Ipswich 0-2 Bournemouth (Davis own goal, 46 mins)
 The second half has started with a bang at Ipswich! An own-bang! Christie shoots from the left of goal, with his left foot and not from a great position, but you don’t win the lottery unless you buy a ticket, and the ball comes off Leif Davis and flies into the net!
 Share 4h ago 09.56 EST “I haven’t seen the hands to the face, I’m busy cooking and with no TV in the kitchen I can’t watch but am just following here,” writes George Ronczy. “If Andres was hit in the neck and grabbed his forehead, he should get booked for simulation.” Absolute and complete agreement from me: the officials may decide that Igor Thiago’s push was violent enough to deserve a red card, it seemed harsh to me but an argument can be made for it. However Andres certainly overdramatised the situation and there should be repercussions for that also.
 Also, what’s on the menu?
